site.name: Physics Playground
site.tagline: Physics experiments you can play with right in your browser.
site.description: Interactive physics simulations for students: free fall, a spring launcher, a draining bucket and an electric field. Nothing to install.

home.heroText: Pick an experiment, change anything you like and see what happens. On Earth, on Mars or on the Moon.
home.heroCanvasLabel: A ball falls to the ground. The faint circles show where the ball was every quarter of a second.

sim.comingSoonText: We're moving it from Python to the website. Until then, you can see the original version on GitHub.

free-fall.title: Free fall
free-fall.blurb: A heavy object and a light one are dropped together. Which lands first?

spring-launcher.title: Spring launcher
spring-launcher.blurb: Squeeze the spring, pick an angle and launch the ball. How far does it go?

freeFall.airNoteEarth: Earth's air at sea level: 1.225 kg/m³.
freeFall.airNoteMoon: The Moon has no air, so this changes nothing.
freeFall.airWarning: Air is on, so the formula is no longer exact.
freeFall.resultAlmost: Same to 1/100 s: the air here is thin.
freeFall.noteReady: Press Drop to draw the graphs.
freeFall.noteNoAtmosphere: No atmosphere here, so the air switch changes nothing.
freeFall.noteAir: Air on: the lighter ball levels off at its top speed.
freeFall.noteLanded: Both lines are exactly on top of each other.
freeFall.noteFalling: Watch one line: the other is hidden underneath it.
freeFall.sceneLabel: Two balls dropped side by side from {h} m.
freeFall.whatText: Earth pulls harder on the heavy ball, but the heavy ball is also harder to get moving. The two effects cancel exactly, so without air everything falls at the same rate: t = √(2h/g). There's no mass in that formula!
freeFall.shortcutsText: Space: drop / pause · R: reset · A: air · 1/2/3: world · + / −: speed

spring.landed: Landed {d} m away after {t} s, exactly as the formula predicted!
spring.ready: The ball is sitting on the squeezed spring. Press Launch!
spring.noteReady: Press Launch! to draw the graphs.
spring.noteEnergy: The red (total) line is flat: energy is never lost, it just swaps between motion and height.
spring.noteVelocity: vx stays the same the whole flight; only vy changes: it goes up, reaches zero at the top, then down.
spring.sceneLabel: A spring launcher fires a ball at {a}°.
spring.whatText: A squeezed spring stores energy: E = ½·k·x². Let go, and all of it becomes the ball's motion: ½·m·v² = E. In the air, gravity only changes the up-and-down speed; the sideways speed stays the same. The total energy stays the same all the time: it just moves between motion and height.
spring.shortcutsText: Space: launch / pause · R: reset · V: speed arrows · 1/2/3: world · + / −: speed

bucket.ready: The hole has a plug in it. Press Pull the plug!
bucket.emptyAfter: Empty after {t}. The first half of the water took {a}, the second half {b}: {r} times slower!
bucket.noteReady: Pull the plug to draw the graphs.
bucket.noteRun: The height falls fast at first, then slower and slower. The jet speed falls in a straight line: v = √(2gh).
bucket.sceneLabel: A bucket with {v} litres of water and a {d} mm hole near the bottom.
bucket.whatText: Water leaves the hole at v = √(2gh), where h is the height of water above the hole (Torricelli's law). More water pushes harder, so the jet is faster. As the bucket empties, h drops and the jet slows down. That's why the second half of the water takes much longer than the first.
bucket.shortcutsText: Space: pull the plug / pause · R: reset · 1/2/3: world · + / −: speed
